notes: Live transcription moves to AssemblyAI Universal-Streaming, so words appear as they are spoken and come back more accurate on accented and overlapping speech. When the transcription service drops mid-meeting the recording is no longer lost — the applet reconnects and keeps the audio, instead of ending the meeting with nothing to show. Speakers the service can separate but not name now read as "Speaker A", "Speaker B" and so on rather than blank labels. Action items that say "tomorrow" or "next Friday" resolve against the day the meeting actually happened. The menubar LIVE row shows the meeting you are recording instead of whichever all-day event happened to be on the calendar. Accepting a meeting from the calendar pill opens one browser tab, not two. The update prompt stops reappearing once you have already updated. Two panels are back in Settings: Release notes, and the Activity log under Diagnostics.

The notes pop-up now appears three minutes before every scheduled meeting on your calendar and stays put until you click into it or ten minutes past the meeting's start — no more scrambling to find the Join button after the call has begun. Signed-in users always get cloud transcription, even without a personal AI key, so notes come back in seconds instead of after a half-hour of local processing. Deleting a note keeps you where you were in the list instead of jumping you back to the top. Solo calls no longer show a false "nobody is being captured" warning. Windows users see Windows-appropriate copy on permission prompts instead of macOS-only settings text. Behind the scenes: opt-in Windows microphone status watcher for tighter permission handling.

Signing in now populates your Pulses, Projects, and Tasks counts right away instead of leaving them blank until the next refresh, and the applet no longer loops on "please sign in again" when the connection is slow. Meeting notes get three fixes: renaming one speaker never accidentally splices into an attendee's full name, foreign-language subtitle noise from quiet meetings is dropped from transcripts, and your own lines read "You" even when your voice went through the system channel instead of the mic. The meeting-detect pill picks the meeting that just started over long in-progress blocks and lets you switch when several overlap; it also pops even when the notes window is already open. New Granola-style tray dropdown shows today and tomorrow's meetings with a quick-nav row. Action items are editable in place before you push them to BuildFactory. On Windows: proper visible tray icon, taskbar unread badge, Start-at-Login toggle, and installers are now signed with a DigiCert EV certificate so SmartScreen stops warning about them.

Closing and reopening your Mac no longer signs you out — the biggest reliability annoyance of the last version is fixed. Notes without a title now get a short, meaningful headline written automatically from what the meeting was about. Long meetings with more than one topic are broken into named sections per topic, plus separate Decisions and Action Items, instead of one long flat list. The notes writing area now fills the whole window and grows with what you type, so nothing gets clipped into a tiny box. Your end-of-day briefing now comes from the same place as your morning one, and matches what you see on the BuildFactory website. Behind the scenes: opt-in backup of your notes to your BuildFactory account is now available for early testing.
Restores meeting detection, automatic recording stop, and live speaker names, which 0.2.36 shipped without. Also makes briefing failures explain themselves instead of failing silently.
First fully automated release. Known issue, fixed in 0.2.37: this build shipped without meeting detection, automatic recording stop, and live speaker names. Update as soon as 0.2.37 appears.

The wave-icon briefing now shows the exact same daily briefing as your BuildFactory Home page, generated by the platform, so it works without a personal AI key and never shows a raw error again. Morning briefings use it too.

Recordings now stop on their own shortly after your meeting ends (and when your Mac sleeps), instead of running until you remember. Meeting popups show the meeting's name instead of a truncated app name, and you get one notification per meeting, not two. The record button is now a green button that says Record. Cloud transcription is more reliable: an expired session refreshes and retries instead of silently falling back.

One sign-in now signs you in everywhere: log in from Notes and the whole applet lights up, log out and every window knows. Embedded Tasks, Builds, and Projects screens no longer lose their session mid-use. Recording is calmer: a live green level meter shows the meeting is being captured and the stop button is small and quiet. New installs are asked to allow notifications at the end of setup instead of one minute before their first meeting.

Your meetings are now un-losable: recorded audio is saved to disk the moment a recording stops and kept until a transcript exists, so a failed transcription can be retried with one click instead of losing the meeting. Fixed the bug that kept signing everyone out; if a session does expire, you get a real notification instead of silence. Notes now asks you to sign in to BuildFactory before use, remembers your email, and works with password managers.

Transcription no longer depends on your own AI account. BuildFactory now transcribes through the BuildFactory service first, falls back to a personal key if you have one, and to on-device transcription otherwise. If an AI account ever runs out of credits, it switches to on-device immediately and tells you, instead of retrying quietly and leaving you without a transcript. Also includes updated AI libraries and reliability fixes from the last few weeks.

Fixes a crash: if a meeting was detected while your Notes window was open, BuildFactory could quit with an error dialog. That is fixed, and the app now recovers from unexpected errors instead of closing, so a fault can no longer end a recording in progress.

Recordings stop on their own again when your call ends, even if another app like Slack is still using your microphone. If BuildFactory ever cannot hear the other side, the Fix permission step now relaunches the app for you, which is what macOS actually requires for a new screen recording permission to take effect. Builds created from a note are also filed under the right project again.

The note header no longer overlaps itself when the transcript panel is open. Settings is also clearer about what runs where: cloud includes cloud transcription, and On this Mac keeps everything on-device so no meeting audio ever leaves your Mac.

Important fix: a background helper that detects when you are on a call was not shutting down with the app, so copies built up over time and could drive your Mac's CPU hard. They now exit properly, and this update cleans up any left behind. If your fans have been loud, this is why.

Fixes chips that could stop opening. Switching quickly between Tasks, Builds and Projects now always opens the one you clicked last, and if a window ever gets stuck the app recovers on its own instead of needing a restart.

Meeting attendees now show as people, not email addresses, everywhere they appear: the attendee list, the people editor, and the summaries themselves. Names come from your BuildFactory directory when the person has an account, and are derived from their address when they do not.

Your edits to a meeting summary are now protected: renaming a speaker or switching templates will never overwrite writing you did by hand. You can also ask the AI to rewrite a follow-up email with your own instruction, like "make it shorter" or "mention the Friday deadline", as many times as you want. Includes a security hardening fix for how saved sign-ins are stored on your Mac.

Action items grew up: assign any item to a meeting attendee from a dropdown, set due dates with a date picker, and once an item becomes a BuildFactory task the row shows In BuildFactory and jumps straight to it. Delegating a task automatically keeps you watching it. You can also fix a mishearing right in the transcript (double-click the line) and carry the fix through the whole note in one tap. Plus various fixes.

Action items now become assigned tasks: the owner on an action item is matched to your company directory, so creating the task assigns it to the right person automatically. Adding people to a meeting got smarter too; type a name or email and they are matched and linked to their BuildFactory account, showing their real name everywhere.

Create builds right from a note: pick a project, choose + New build, and the note files itself under it. Back-to-back calls now get separate notes; hopping from Teams to a Slack huddle ends the first recording and offers a fresh one. First-meeting transcription is much faster; the model now readies itself in the background when Notes opens.

Teams calls now name who is speaking in real time (keep the participants panel open). The transcript panel opens only when you ask and sits beside your notes instead of covering them. Copied summaries keep their formatting when pasted into Slack, Gmail, or Notion.

Your typed notes and the AI summary are now one document: everything you write during a meeting appears in the finished notes, in your words, expanded with detail from the transcript. Your original typed notes stay one click away.

Meeting detection now covers Slack huddles and Teams, so the take-notes offer appears no matter where your call starts. Fixing a name once in your summary now offers to update it everywhere in the note, including the transcript. Release notes are fully scrollable.

Meeting recordings just got more trustworthy: if BuildFactory ever cannot hear the other side of your call, a banner now tells you immediately, with a one-click permission fix, instead of quietly recording only your microphone.

Getting started is now one step: the welcome tour begins with your BuildFactory sign-in, and new teammates can create an account right from the tour. The BuildFactory helmet also now sits in your Mac menu bar; click it to open the bar anytime. Plus various fixes.
You can now browse all release notes any time from Settings. Plus various fixes.
Ask across your notes just got sharper: when you name a meeting ("the DSI meeting"), that meeting now leads the answer, even if your question's wording happens to match other meetings better.
Various fixes.
After each update, a small badge appears next to settings. Click it to see what changed and why it matters to you. (You are looking at it right now.)
Various fixes and polish.
New here? Notes now starts with a sample meeting so you can see exactly what a summary looks like before you record your first one.

Ask across your notes now understands meaning, not just keywords. Ask "what did we promise the client?" and it finds the answer even when your notes said it a different way. All of it happens privately on your Mac.
BuildFactory now opens as soon as you launch it, and Pulse cards are cleaner and faster to triage. Plus various fixes.
